chapter_seo_title: RMJI Ch. 256 – The Two Words: A Secret Negotiation in Yanling Fort
chapter_meta_description: Han Li prepares for a trading session in Yanling Fort, but the real storm unfolds when the Yan Clan ancestor meets the Ghost Spirit Sect’s masked young master—and two whispered words shake his composure.
og_title: RMJI Ch. 256 – The Two Words That Shook a Core Formation Patriarch
og_description: While Han Li focuses on practical preparation, the Ghost Spirit Sect delivers a secret that forces an overnight negotiation.
twitter_title: RMJI 256 – Two Words That Broke a Patriarch’s Calm
twitter_description: The Yan Clan ancestor meets the Ghost Spirit Sect. Two whispered words change everything.

lore_anchors.definition: A major demonic sect known for commanding ghosts, poisons, and shadow techniques; part of the Six Demonic Sects of Tianluo Nation.
The third major cultivation realm; cultivators at this level can form a golden core in their dantian and possess significantly greater lifespan and combat power.
The central command building of Yanling Fort, used by the Yan Clan for high-level decision-making and meetings.
An honorific title for the oldest and most powerful cultivator of a clan, often a Core Formation or higher existence who serves as the clan’s ultimate deterrent.
A common storage medium in cultivation fiction; contains information that can be read with spiritual sense.
A pair of notorious Core Formation cultivators known for their mismatched appearances and fearsome reputation; they serve as bodyguards to the Ghost Spirit Sect’s young master.
A heavily sealed room with layered restrictions and formation barriers designed to prevent eavesdropping by cultivators or spiritual sense probes.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What are the 'two words' the masked young master says to the Yan Clan patriarch?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The text deliberately leaves them unsaid. It is a narrative hook that suggests a hidden secret—either a name, a location, or an event—powerful enough to force a Core Formation cultivator into immediate negotiation.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why do the cultivators suddenly stop talking about the Ghost Spirit Sect?
cultural_notes_faq.a: In a world where private information is currency, openly discussing a dangerous faction is a risk. The group's shift to cultivation techniques is a deliberate de-escalation, signaling that none of them want to be the one to invite trouble by probing too deeply.

They are a pair of notorious Core Formation cultivators, one appearing ancient and one appearing as a child but speaking with a guttural voice. Their presence signals that the Ghost Spirit Sect has sent high-level combat assets, not just diplomats.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Han Li choose the Wind Joy Inn?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He deliberately selects an obscure inn near the city wall to minimize distractions and keep an escape route close. This is consistent with his survival-first mindset, especially after learning of the Ghost Spirit Sect's presence.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does the Yan Clan ancestor refuse to take the letter immediately?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He is testing the masked young master's composure and intent. By forcing the young master to reveal his hidden card (the two words) before reading the letter, he ensures he enters the negotiation with full context, not blind trust.
